subject: Culture
title: Amazon Wishlists
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Amazon Wishlists.

hook.text: Amazon's wishlist feature accounts for $1 billion in annual gift sales. You now tell people what to buy you.

buildup.text: Wishlists eliminate surprise but maximize utility. The recipient always gets what they want.

discovery.text: Psychologists found that givers overvalue surprise while receivers prefer getting what they asked for.

twist.text: But receiving exactly what you listed kills the emotional bonus of feeling understood by another person.

climax.text: The best-selling Amazon wishlist items are gift cards—gifts stripped of all personal meaning.

punchline.text: Efficiency solved gifting and killed its magic at the same time.

quiz.question: What is the top-selling item on Amazon wishlists?
